name: Franchise Networks
summary: Central control, allocation and entity-aware operations.

hero.subheadText: Give head office the visibility to plan and allocate while each outlet keeps responsibility for its own operation.

heroImage.alt: Franchise retail manager reviewing inventory in a contemporary Indian store.

painsIntro.title: Networks need central discipline without blurring outlet boundaries.
painsIntro.lede: Five tensions between head-office governance and store-level operating autonomy.

pains.title: Every outlet has a different operating context
pains.body: A network needs one view without treating all locations as the same entity.

pains.title: Central standards can blur local ownership
pains.body: Head office control must not remove the responsibility that belongs at an outlet.

pains.title: Allocation decisions need live context
pains.body: Stock needs to move to the right outlet with clear source, destination and ownership.

pains.title: Plans and subscriptions need network discipline
pains.body: Partner operating context needs to remain clear as the network evolves.

pains.title: Consolidation cannot erase boundaries
pains.body: Network visibility is useful only when entity-level records and books remain distinct.

fit.title: Centralize the rules and visibility. Keep ownership where it belongs.
fit.body: Bizonix connects head-office planning to outlet operations without mixing entities or their records.

floatingBannerBottomRight.title: Every piece, one identity
floatingBannerBottomRight.subtitle: Receipt to counter, on one record

painsIntro.title: Imitation jewellery demands precision a basic item code cannot provide.
painsIntro.lede: Five operational pressures that make jewellery retail fragile without piece-level control.

pains.title: Design-heavy SKUs quickly lose their structure
pains.body: Small variations across collections make a simple product list difficult to trust.

pains.title: Piece-level certainty is hard to maintain
pains.body: A piece needs to remain identifiable from supplier receipt through display, sale and return.

pains.title: Supplier receiving can fragment the record
pains.body: GRN context and physical pieces need to arrive together, not be reconciled later.

pains.title: The counter cannot wait for the back office
pains.body: Fast POS needs to stay connected to the exact piece that has just moved.

pains.title: Movement needs a traceable identity
pains.body: Transfers, returns and location changes should not separate a piece from its operating history.

fit.title: A connected operating path for every piece—from receipt to sale.
fit.body: Bizonix links piece identity, supplier context and counter movement into one usable operating view.

name: Apparel & Footwear
summary: Size, colour, season and piece-aware operations.

hero.subheadText: Hold the size and colour grid together across store, warehouse and partner, so a style reads the same everywhere it is stocked.

secondaryCta.label: See it on a real style

heroImage.alt: Apparel retail team reviewing stock across sizes and colourways.

painsIntro.title: Apparel carries more context than a stock number can hold.
painsIntro.lede: Five pressures show up in almost every apparel operation. None of them are solved by counting harder.

pains.title: Variants multiply faster than visibility
pains.body: Size, colour and seasonal ranges make a single stock number too blunt for daily decisions.

pains.title: Stock is not where demand is
pains.body: Warehouse, store and back-room availability can drift apart when movement is handled separately.

pains.title: Franchise sell-through arrives late
pains.body: Partner outlet movement needs to remain visible without taking away local operating responsibility.

pains.title: Wholesale packs need their own logic
pains.body: Pack-level fulfilment has to stay tied to the exact variants that are actually available.

pains.title: Channel movement can tell different stories
pains.body: Retail sales, transfers and wholesale dispatches must resolve into one usable view of stock.

fit.title: One operating view for the pressures apparel teams manage every day.
fit.body: Bizonix connects the workflows around the garment—not just the systems around the business.
